definition: Cross-lingual Understanding — the capability of transferring learned knowledge between languages, typically evaluated on multilingual benchmarks.
details: Cross-lingual Understanding — the capability of transferring learned knowledge between languages, typically evaluated on multilingual benchmarks.

explainer.lead: XLU measures whether a model trained mostly on one language can still handle others. It matters because most training data is English, so transfer is how multilingual products become viable.

tiers.eli5: It is like learning to ride a bike in one country and then finding you can ride a rented bike abroad without lessons.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers zero-shot or fine-tune a multilingual model and score it on parallel multilingual test sets to see how much transfers. A common pitfall is reading high cross-lingual scores as fluency, when they often reflect shared structure and easy task formats.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, XLU is the average task performance on non-source languages after training on a source language, evaluated on multilingual benchmarks; gains depend on shared vocabulary and script overlap, and low-resource languages typically lag.

explainer.example: Train a natural language inference model on English data, then evaluate it on the same task translated into 15 languages and report the average accuracy as the cross-lingual transfer score.
